title: Mysterious object from the 1947 Roswell UFO crash site
excerpt: Nearly 80 years after Roswell, a Japanese Buddhist priest reveals an object he claims was found at the 1947 UFO crash site
content:
A mysterious object displayed at a Japanese UFO museum has brought renewed attention to the famous Roswell incident. Takano Josen, a Japanese Buddhist priest and UFO researcher, presented the unusual find during an interview with American journalist Jesse Michels. He believes it was recovered from the location where an unidentified craft allegedly crashed in New Mexico in 1947.

Takano’s account reveals a little-known story behind the discovery. He claims that the commonly identified Roswell crash location is not the actual site. Instead, he points to another area in the New Mexico desert, where the ground reportedly showed signs of a powerful impact.

Takano founded Cosmo Isle Hakui, a space and UFO museum in Japan. During the interview, he explained that Walter Haut and Jesse Marcel Jr. took him to the suspected crash location. Haut was the military public information officer who announced the recovery of a flying disc in July 1947.

🚨BREAKING🚨: Japanese monk claims to have a piece of the Roswell UFO and shows it publicly for the first time. Takano Jousen was friends with the Marcel Family, first responders at the Roswell crash. Through them, and trips to New Mexico, he claims he was able to bring back a piece of the crash. He also claims that close friend, Apollo 17 commander and the last man to walk on the moon, Gene Cernan, told him that he received a telepathic warning to stay off the Moon. Finally, Jousen exposes NASA’s code words for UFOs (“Bogey”, “Skunk”, “Santa Claus”) and claims he personally smuggled UFO footage out of NASA’s Johnson Space Center.

According to Takano, the actual location contained a gouged area several metres across. The group did not bring a metal detector during their visit. However, a friend later returned to the site and recovered pieces of material. He eventually gave one of the recovered pieces to Takano’s museum.

The discovery has particular significance because of descriptions given by Major Jesse Marcel, the intelligence officer who examined the original Roswell debris. He reportedly described an unusual, extremely lightweight material that could be crumpled and then return to its original shape. It was also said to resist fire, prompting comparisons with so-called memory metal.

What exactly fell in the New Mexico desert in July 1947, and what did the military recover from the wreckage?

VIDEO. Roswell – UFO Crash in New Mexico | History.

Almost 80 years later, the circumstances surrounding the incident remain a source of fascination. The mysterious object now displayed in Japan adds another intriguing piece to a story that has never lost its power to capture the imagination.

We previously wrote about the still-mysterious historical mystery of UFO sightings. Scientists are still wondering: What really happened on October 27, 1954? On that distant day, thousands of fans in the stadium during the Fiorentina-Pistoiese match saw a UFO.
